target_customer: Software companies and data teams that want to let their own users query databases in natural language
problem: Business users cannot write SQL, so data questions queue behind analysts; Dataherald offered an embeddable text-to-SQL API and later an open source engine.
business_model: API and enterprise software for NL-to-SQL, with an open source engine released in 2024
product_category: Natural language to SQL, data analytics tooling

founders.name: Amir Zohrenejad
education: UC Berkeley, EECS and Applied Mathematics

founders.name: Anuj Saigal
founders.background_notes: Source: YC company page. Later co-founded Spark AI.

exit.reason: Not stated by the company; PitchBook lists the company as out of business with a status date of 23 Dec 2024.

technical_complexity.rationale: Text-to-SQL needed schema context, confidence scoring and fine tuning on customer data; the LLM wave of 2023 made the core easier to copy but accuracy on messy enterprise schemas stayed hard.

defensibility.rationale: The company open sourced its whole engine in 2024 and foundation model vendors and BI tools could offer the same feature; no data or network moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source documents an incumbent copying Dataherald specifically; the company wound down by late 2024.

market_need_then: Data analytics backlogs and the push for self-serve analytics existed in 2021; the YC page and launch post frame the pain as users unable to get quick answers to data questions. Direct spend evidence not found.

branding.domain_note: dataherald.com, the company's own .com (domain now unreachable).

identity.voice_and_tone: Developer-focused, product launch posts on YC and Product Hunt (Jan 2024).

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launch on 24 Jan 2024 earned 126 upvotes and 8 comments (per search summary); coverage on Hacker News when open sourced in May 2024.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand-specific coverage found; some developer attention at the open source release but no sign the name drove growth.

pivots.from: Earlier Dataherald product (media publisher customers per a job post; details not sourced)
pivots.why: Not stated; YC launch post describes the NL-to-SQL API and open source engine

outcome_analysis: Dataherald went through YC in Winter 2021, raised only a small seed round per databases, then pivoted into text-to-SQL once LLMs made the idea hot. It open sourced the engine in May 2024 and PitchBook marks it out of business in December 2024. The company has not stated a cause, so the failure factors are inferred and weakly supported: crowded text-to-SQL market, small funding and a late pivot.
notes: Website dataherald.com could not be fetched (DNS failure), treated as dead. Funding amounts conflict across databases (VCBacked $2.9M total, PitchBook $2.12M, CB Insights $500K); both recorded rounds rest on a single database each and are unverified. No press release found. Cause of shutdown not public. The pivot date is an estimate from the launch post age; the pre-LLM product is not documented. Competitors: no source dated near Jan 2021 was found, so the list is empty. A startupintros Herald seed result is a different company and was ignored.
